name: IL-09
label: Safe D

key_factors: Open seat after Schakowsky's retirement, but Democrats hold a deep bench
Biss's large fundraising advantage over a lightly funded Republican
Prediction markets price Democratic win near 95%
model.rationale: The seat's D+19 partisan lean and Chicago-area Democratic base make a Republican takeover highly unlikely even with the incumbent retiring. Biss has raised nearly $3 million and drawn heavy outside spending while the Republican campaign shows minimal financial footprint, and markets price a Democratic win around 95%.
model.watch: A primary upset or an unexpectedly strong Republican fundraising surge could narrow the margin, though the district's lean makes an upset very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.

Open seat: Jan Schakowsky (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Jan Schakowsky's retirement leaves this Chicago-area seat open, but the district's D+19 partisan lean keeps it firmly in Democratic hands on paper. Daniel Biss enters the general election with a substantial financial edge, having raised nearly $3 million, while outside groups have spent heavily both for and against him. Republican John Elleson's campaign shows little reported fundraising or outside support.

Prediction markets put the Democratic nominee's chances near 95%, and no expert raters flag the race as competitive. With no general-election polling available, the forecast rests on the district's fundamentals, which point to a comfortable Democratic hold in the mid-twenties margin range.
